purpose: ASVS V7.5.1 requires full re-authentication before modifying account attributes that affect authentication. organization-invitation.service.ts required none for any of its three membership commands. The third is the serious one: resetting another member's MFA is an account-takeover primitive, and a hijacked organization-admin session obtained it with only the role, a rate limit and a version check.
requiredInvariants: The previous record named one command; measurement found three. changeMembershipRole, revokeMembership and resetMembershipMfa all lacked any freshness check, and all three are gated now.

The gate runs FIRST, before the administrator is even resolved. The behavioural spec stubs everything the command would touch afterwards to throw a plain Error, so a ForbiddenException in the result proves the ordering rather than asserting it in prose.

The control is stated once. The same check already existed five times in the tree, redeclared in each place and in TWO different meanings - some allow 30 seconds of forward clock skew, some reject any negative age. The new call site takes a shared module with the meaning written down instead of picking one by accident.

The five existing call sites are NOT rewritten in this pass. That is a separate refactor with its own regression risk across settlement and staff-access; the divergence is recorded as a finding rather than removed in passing.
The refusal code is FRESH_MFA_REQUIRED, identical to what the existing sites already return, so a client cannot distinguish the new gate from the old ones.

One line was REMOVED from the control because it could not be proven: the Number.isFinite check was redundant, since an unreadable timestamp yields NaN and every comparison with NaN is false. A mutation deleting it failed no test. An unprovable line in a security control is worse than its absence; the property is pinned by a test instead.

No dependency, schema, migration, RLS or policy change. No registration business logic, 1C, marketing or presentation code. No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.

The two cryptographic-inventory files are regenerated, never hand-edited. discover-cryptography.mjs writes the .json and the .md together and its staleness test reads the pair; adding source files moves scannedFiles, so both are regenerated here and neither is touched by hand.
acceptance: Measured before changing anything: organization-invitation.service.ts contained zero occurrences of any freshness check across its three membership commands.

Six mutations of the control and its call sites were run, each verified to have applied: removing the gate from one command, from all three, accepting an unconfirmed factor, accepting any future timestamp, widening the window to a day - all five turn the suite red. The sixth, removing the isFinite guard, changed nothing, which is why that line was deleted rather than kept.

V7.5.1 PASS is machine-revocable: four mutations with the matrix rebuilt each time - removing all three gates, untracking the behavioural spec, dropping the clock-skew bound, and weakening the ordering assertion - all four drive the verdict to NOT_ASSESSED.
Matrix on this head: PASS 129 -> 130, FAIL 90 -> 89. Exactly one verdict changed; no collateral drift.
Full @pc/api suite: 2893 passed, 0 failed. scripts/security suite green.
